As a multitude of nations mobilize to intervene in Western Shamat, a simple recon flight of two Luso Mk.5s (a light attack jet similar to the Dragonfly and Alpha jet) zip over Sal-Baliz and natural towns. As the specialized optical pods attached to the planes hardpoints scan the ground, each taking thermal and normal images faster than a man can blink, the lead plane gets a message on his RWR that jolts the pilot to full alert. It's a radar lock, presumably from some self propelled anti-aircraft system from the 50's. They the Sal always do this when they do recon flights, but it still creeps him out it bit. "Maybe it's a sign of things to come" he thinks to himself, yet as routine, he keeps flying and the RWR stops screaming at him indicating that the SPAA lost track of him.

As workers speed around a shady office, sorting files for shipments of illegal goods and funding for organizations that the public doesn't think too highly of, a small letter is found at the entrance to the office. This isn't something that the mailman dropped off, hell, this part of the building doesn't even have an address. A worker brings it to his boss, and it reads as follows:

[i]Dear Sir or Madam working for [nation]Sikirsk[/nation]...[/i]
Diplomacy is a tricky matter, yes? Much like business i'd say. Now, if your nation of smugglers wishes to keep making money from "disappearing" items that are a bit of a bother for our army to get rid of officially, no funding shall be sent to any who operate in Lavian territory. This is a simple message, and I hope you understand our bit of strongarming in this business, but our bosses would both prefer to keep crime out of Lavia and bombs out of your buildings.

Signed: [b]SIC[/b]
